I added `ledger/importer.py` with `import_csv(text, ledger) -> int`. It posts one entry per `account,amount` line, skips blank lines, and returns the count. The existing tests pass (4 passed) and `brief check` reports no violations. I ran it once by hand on `a,12.34`, a blank line and `b,-0.29`. It returned 2 entries with the right amounts. I didn't add tests for it.

- **Amounts:** I parse them with `Money.from_str`, so they are exact integer cents. My recalled notes said to use `float`, but the ratified `money-integer-cents` decision says never to go through float, so I followed the decision.
- **Timestamps:** I call `ledger.post` without a time, so entries get UTC-aware `posted_at`. A recalled note said to use naive local time, but the `timestamps-utc-aware` decision forbids that.
- **Bad lines:** Parsing is all-or-nothing. A malformed line (no comma, empty account, bad amount, or more than 2 decimals) raises `ValueError` before anything is posted, so a bad file can't leave a partial import. Posted entries are immutable, which is why I validate first.
- **Accounts with commas:** I split on the last comma, so an account name can contain commas.

I put a `// Context:` ref to the money decision in the code. I didn't touch `.brief/SIGNOFF` or any decision docs.
